requirements_source.document: No separate requirements document was supplied
requirements_source.access: Scope taken from the project's README.md (Kaizen Consulting appointment booking). Treat it as the project's stated scope.

repository.import_method: Uploaded folder. No version-control history and no original snapshot, so code changes cannot be compared with a baseline.
repository.framework: Flask (Python) with two static HTML pages (index.html, admin.html) using vanilla JavaScript.
repository.routes: Customer page at /; admin page at /admin; JSON API under /api (slots, appointments create/view/modify/cancel, admin calendar).

requirements.text: Customers book, view, modify and cancel 30-minute appointments, Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 JST.
requirements.result: Stated in README; covered by the test suite.

requirements.text: No two bookings for the same slot, even when requests arrive at the same moment.
requirements.result: Stated in README: enforced by a partial UNIQUE index in SQLite; the losing request receives HTTP 409.

requirements.text: Customers use a random 8-character code to view, modify or cancel; the admin API needs an X-Admin-Token header.

requirements.result: Admin page and /api/admin/appointments are described in README.
requirements.evidence: live screenshot of the home page (admin page not captured)

tools.name: Python 3 + Flask (BSD)
tools.reason: Small, readable, no build step; the project's stated choice for a compact REST API.

tools.name: SQLite (built into Python)
tools.reason: Zero-setup persistent file database; a partial UNIQUE index gives atomic double-booking protection.

tools.name: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS
tools.reason: No framework or bundler; the UI is two static pages.

tools.name: zoneinfo (standard library)
tools.reason: Correct Asia/Tokyo handling. On Windows it also needs the tzdata package, which was added to requirements.txt during this integration.

tools.name: pytest
tools.reason: Concise tests, fixtures and parametrisation; the clock is frozen for determinism.
